liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (2 reviews): The reviewer says the Sugaree alone is worth the admission price; Sugaree is described as smoking [31][35]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): The reviewer singles out Little Red Rooster as a blistering version [26]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Feel Like A Stranger had a different groove, with Jerry and Philip interacting before the closing transition and crescendo [30]
- **Far From Me** (1 review): Far From Me is singled out as especially good [30]
- **Althea** (1 review): Althea is named the best song, with Jerry sweetly leading the band through it [30]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Not Fade Away, coming out of Space, is praised for having no annoying crowd clapping [31]
- **Alabama Getaway** (1 review): The reviewer counts the Alabama Getaway among their favorite versions [35]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd80-09-06 s1t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [36]
- **gd80-09-06 s1t02 Alabama Getaway**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [36]
- **gd80-09-06 s1t03 Greatest Story Ever Told**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [36]
- **gd80-09-06 s1t04 Sugaree**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [36]
- **gd80-09-06 s1t05 Me & My Uncle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [36]
- **gd80-09-06 s1t06 Mexicali Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [36]
- **gd80-09-06 s1t07 Tennessee Jed**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [36]
- **gd80-09-06 s1t08 Feel Like A Stranger**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [36]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-09-06.142972.fob.nak700.wise.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 31 songs; 212 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd80-09-06.sbd_aud.miller.25560.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 28 songs; 216 min; rated 4.47/5 by 43 [3]. Said about its sound: The soundboard runs somewhat slow compared with how the reviewer remembers the show; The matrix tape sounds remarkably clear but seems short on bass [28][29]
- **gd1980-09-06.147840.fob.shure.sm57.sublette.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 28 songs; 213 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [9]
- **gd80-09-06.wise.unknown.322.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 29 songs; 210 min; rated 4.14/5 by 28 [11]. Said about its sound: The audience tape has the crowd clapping along to the rhythm so much that the reviewer finds it excessive; This audience copy suffers from wind distortion and oversaturation, and the reviewer wants a better-sounding one [25][27]
- **gd80-09-06.set1-sbd.samaritano.23371.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 107 min; rated 4.62/5 by 8 [22]
- **gd1980-09-06.175072.tape1.sbd.remaster.browning.samaritano.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 10 songs; 88 min [23]

## Around the show

- The reviewer describes the show as hot, played on a nice day [27]
- An attendee recalls the show as very upbeat and among the best they ever saw [28]
- A gorgeous fall day with a happy crowd, and Levon was part of the day [31]
- Six people drove up from Vassar in a 1976 Pacer; the day had frisbees and Labor Day sunburns [32]
- The reviewer danced through the set, and at one point the clouds parted so shafts of sunlight beamed down [33]
- Roy Bucanan and then Levon Helm opened the show [1]
- The reviewer ranks this among the top shows of 1980 [35]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-09-06.142972.fob.nak700.wise.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Jim Wise's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII-C90)(patched out of Steve Rolfe);… [1]. Also: Jim Wise recorded the show; this release uses a fresh transfer of his Nakamichi 700 FOB source [1]
- **gd80-09-06.sbd_aud.miller.25560.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience composite [3]
- **gd1980-09-06.147840.fob.shure.sm57.sublette.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Kathy Sublette; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Kathy Sublette's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Shure SM57 mics > Sony-TC158 [9]. Also: A 38-second patch in Drums comes from Jim Wise's Nakamichi 700 FOB source [9]
- **gd80-09-06.wise.unknown.322.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [11]
- **gd80-09-06.set1-sbd.samaritano.23371.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Joe Samaritano; source: Soundboard [22]. Also: On this soundboard source, the last three tracks of the first set are audience-recording material [26]
- **gd1980-09-06.175072.tape1.sbd.remaster.browning.samaritano.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Tape provided by Joey Browning Transfer by Joe Samaritano Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 6, 2025; source: SBD > Cassette Master > ? > Cassette > SHN > FLAC [23]. Also: This is a remaster of the shnid 25560 soundboard, with the vocal phase issue and pitch repaired and a patch added; The patch was supplied by Scott Clugston, Jim Wise and Steve Rolfe; this is the only soundboard available [23]

claims.text: The audience tape has the crowd clapping along to the rhythm so much that the reviewer finds it excessive
On this soundboard source, the last three tracks of the first set are audience-recording material
The reviewer singles out Little Red Rooster as a blistering version
This audience copy suffers from wind distortion and oversaturation, and the reviewer wants a better-sounding one
The reviewer describes the show as hot, played on a nice day
An attendee recalls the show as very upbeat and among the best they ever saw
The soundboard runs somewhat slow compared with how the reviewer remembers the show
The matrix tape sounds remarkably clear but seems short on bass
Feel Like A Stranger had a different groove, with Jerry and Philip interacting before the closing transition and crescendo
Far From Me is singled out as especially good
Althea is named the best song, with Jerry sweetly leading the band through it
The reviewer says the Sugaree alone is worth the admission price
A gorgeous fall day with a happy crowd, and Levon was part of the day
Not Fade Away, coming out of Space, is praised for having no annoying crowd clapping
Six people drove up from Vassar in a 1976 Pacer; the day had frisbees and Labor Day sunburns
The reviewer danced through the set, and at one point the clouds parted so shafts of sunlight beamed down
The reviewer counts the Alabama Getaway among their favorite versions
Sugaree is described as smoking
The reviewer ranks this among the top shows of 1980
Roy Bucanan and then Levon Helm opened the show
Jim Wise recorded the show; this release uses a fresh transfer of his Nakamichi 700 FOB source
Sourced from Kathy Sublette's master audience cassettes, recorded with Shure SM57 microphones; Charlie Miller did the transfer
A 38-second patch in Drums comes from Jim Wise's Nakamichi 700 FOB source
This is a remaster of the shnid 25560 soundboard, with the vocal phase issue and pitch repaired and a patch added
The patch was supplied by Scott Clugston, Jim Wise and Steve Rolfe; this is the only soundboard available
